chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, raised it from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When a man has intercourse with a woman in her anus, if he does not discharge semen, there is no ritual bath (ghusl) upon either of them; and if he does discharge, then the ritual bath is upon him, and there is no ritual bath upon her.
ai.seo_question: Is ghusl required for both partners after anal intercourse if the man ejaculates?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the specific conditions for ritual purity (ghusl) following anal intercourse, distinguishing between ejaculation and non-ejaculation. It highlights the Shia scholarly view that the obligation of ghusl for the man is contingent upon the emission of semen, while the woman remains exempt regardless of the man's state, emphasizing the asymmetry in ritual requirements for this act.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Barqy, 
(It has been narrated) raising it from Abu Abullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The man goes to the woman into her behind, but does not discharge, so there is no washing upon the two of them, and if he does discharges, so upon him is the washing, and there is no washing upon her’.
en.sarwar: 8. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Barqiy in a marfu‘ manner who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

If a man allows intercourse to take place in a woman’s anus without discharge of semen, Ghusl (bath) is not necessary on neither one of them, but if he discharges, Ghusl (bath) is necessary on him but it is not necessary on the woman.’”
